note: Decision lineage for the Harness² field test, 19 Oct 2026 (IST). Types: ask = user request, decision, finding, bug, amendment (to PREREG.md).

events.title: Test Harness² hands-on
events.what: Understand google-research/harness2, take cues from a demo video, research with Perplexity and Context7, preflight, design and run benchmarks, explain it with archify and an HTML report, with Claude Code use cases.

events.title: Compare with Karpathy's autoresearch
events.what: Added a grader-in-the-loop keep-if-better baseline on the same harness surface.

events.title: Context7 has no harness2 docs
events.what: Context7 indexes unrelated 'harness' libraries only, so the cloned repo became the primary reference. Context7 was used later for Google ADK (it surfaced the ollama_chat gotcha).

events.title: Cost model: 4k rollouts + 3k improver stages per task
events.what: Read from recursion.py. The improver already supports a claude_cli channel, which made a Claude-driven test possible.

events.title: No official benchmarks: the only GCP project is production
events.what: LAB, JobBench and WorkBuddy need Vertex Gemini. The only gcloud project is a production project, so it stayed untouched. We built our own benchmark instead.
events.why: Never bill or touch a production project for experiments.

events.title: Use a custom agent, no secret accounts
events.what: Build an ADK-based agent if Claude Code can't be used; find any way to test.

events.title: Second executor: Google ADK on local qwen3:8b
events.what: Ollama from the official GitHub release, no account. ADK via LiteLLM with the ollama_chat provider (from Context7). This mirrors the video's 'mid-tier model plus a better harness' claim.
events.why: No API keys or extra accounts; a weak model gives headroom.

events.title: Nested Claude runs loaded the user's 60+ MCP servers and hooks
events.what: Isolated with --setting-sources project plus an empty strict MCP config: 31k-token context, about 3 s startup, no user hooks.

events.title: Adversarial review and security review before the benchmark
Claude Code + Haiku 5.5 at ceiling (18/18)
events.what: The first easy-only benchmark leaves no headroom, and the ADK runs crashed on a missing mcp module.

events.title: Add difficulty tiers, SWE-style tasks
Rebuild as 3 domains x 3 tiers
events.what: data, ops and swe at easy, medium and hard. Hard tiers hide rules in POLICY.md or RUNBOOK.md; SWE tiers are multi-file repos with hidden regression tests.

events.title: qwen3 at 18 tok/s with thinking on
events.what: Flash attention gave 27 tok/s. Later we found the /no_think tag is ignored via LiteLLM; only think=False works.

events.title: Still at ceiling with tiers: CC 27/27
events.what: Leak audit clean (no grader reads). CC becomes the negative control; ADK carries the headroom question.

events.title: zen has no model keys: run the three review stances as Claude subagents
events.what: Critical, supportive and neutral reviewers read the code directly.
events.why: Keep the skill's method when its tool is unavailable.

events.title: Surface name 'hpb' disables every Harness² edit
events.what: harness2's prompt builder only knows opencode and codex. Every proposal would raise and fall back to base, so the result would silently read 'Harness² = base'.

events.title: Agents could read graders and answers on disk
events.what: Workspaces sat next to hpb/ and to earlier pilot answers; trajectories leaked absolute paths.

events.title: Secrets in agent environment
events.what: GITHUB_TOKEN and three API keys were passed to claude --dangerously-skip-permissions.

events.title: Impossible data and grader flaws
events.what: Refunds dated before settlement, chargebacks before capture, a test-customer rule that never fired, a forgeable stdout grader, valid_json counted as credit, an out-of-scope hidden test.

events.title: macOS sandbox-exec plus env allow-list for every model process
events.what: Deny reads of graders, experiments and credential dirs; deny writes outside the workspace; no web tools; no session persistence.

events.title: Pre-register endpoints and the leak rule
events.what: Primary endpoint per executor, bootstrap + sign-flip, failure handling, and 'any instance literal in a harness voids the cell'.

events.title: A1: ADK aborted runs on tool exceptions
events.what: Tools now return ERROR text as an observation; ADK arm discarded and relaunched.

events.title: A2: host load ~200, fewer ADK re-rolls
events.what: EDR, syspolicyd and Spotlight saturated the CPU. ADK re-rolls cut to R=3/R=2; base kept at R=4.

events.title: A3: drop ADK sequential k=2
events.what: Freed local GPU time for the primary comparison.

events.title: Login failures counted as agent failures
events.what: Concurrent CLI starts returned 'Not logged in' with subtype=success (11 of 237 rollouts, 4 improver sessions), producing a fake +0.11 Harness² gain on Claude Code. Exposed by an A/A check: autoresearch's frozen harness equalled base yet scored higher.

events.title: A4: classify auth failures as infra, re-run the CC arm
events.what: Whole CC arm re-run from clean derived state; the improver retries auth with backoff.

events.title: Clean CC result: Harness² keeps base on 9/9
events.what: Every condition scores 1.0. Harness² proposes edits, then composes back to the base harness. Negative control passed.

events.title: ADK: +0.74 in-task, +0.81 on fresh data, +0.02 transfer
events.what: Weak model goes from mostly failing to 3/3 on 6 of 8 tasks; gains hold on unseen instances; no carry-over to harder tiers.

events.title: The improver wrote answers into the harness
events.what: Ops skills recorded the exact expected values as 'workspace facts'; data skills carried instance ids. 6 of 8 in-task cells void under the pre-registered rule; on the 2 clean tasks the gain is +0.33. harness2's guard checks grader verdicts, not computed answers.

events.title: Report all three numbers, not the flattering one
events.what: As-run, strict (voided cells removed), and fresh-seed variants. Variants cannot leak by construction.

events.title: Follow-up: leak guard plus hook component, ADK rerun
events.what: validate_tree rejects harnesses with the task's answers or ids; a hook forces output/ before finishing (the data-e-v failure printed the right answer instead of writing it).

events.title: Compare with a second video run
events.what: A Gemini 3.5 Flash run on a LAB legal task went from 20/55 to 22/55, with one model doing job, fix and grade.

events.title: Four gaps: self-improvement, no-probe ablation, library on/off, official tasks
events.what: Our improver was stronger than the agents; we never tested the paper's 'probe before adopting' claim, never isolated the library, and never ran Google's own tasks. Two follow-up sessions opened.

events.title: Leak guard works: voided in-task cells 6/8 → 0/9
events.what: With guard v1 plus the c8 Stop hook, ADK in-task +0.65 (8 up, 0 down) and fresh-seed variants +0.97 (6/6 up). The one remaining flag was a policy constant ($15.00) colliding with a count.

events.title: Docker Desktop woken by a status check; load average 409
events.what: A `docker ps` run to answer 'are you using Docker?' started Docker Desktop's VM (224% CPU). Together with about 16 parallel Haiku rollouts, user hooks timed out. Quit Docker; asked both sessions to cap concurrency at 4.

events.title: Leak prevention in depth (guard v2 + audit + held-out headline)
events.what: hpb/leakguard.py adds data, entity and verbatim checks; a read-only audit covers every arm; the LAB session was asked to wire it in, since its guard only blocked fact phrasing; fresh/held-out results become the headline.

events.title: git init opened a new leak path: .git readable from the sandbox
events.what: Committing the project put the graders (hpb/bench.py) and results into .git, which the sandbox did not deny. Agents do run `git log` in their workspaces. Exposure window 12:28–13:20. No exec stream shows git show, cat-file or a grep of graders. LAB rubric text was never committed (eval rows hold criterion ids and pass/fail only). Fix: deny ROOT/.git in sandboxed().

events.title: Claude CLI OAuth expired machine-wide; a second classifier gap
events.what: Every claude -p call returned 'Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired'. That string was not in the infra list, so rollouts would have scored as agent failures. Added to AUTH_FAIL; no recorded result was affected. LAB paused.

events.title: Approve the full held-out LAB matrix at R=3 (~$144)
events.what: After a re-login. The first status check still read loggedIn false from this app's environment; a second check confirmed true, and an isolated nested run returned PONG before anything was spent.

events.title: LAB final: held-out +6.9 pts, Haiku self-improver −4.1
events.what: Adopted Sonnet harnesses on matters their improver never saw: +0.069 over 12 cells (+0.059 without the leaky one). Concentrated in redline-to-redline transfer and partly format alignment with the judge's reader. Haiku improving itself lost ground (demo task 33.3 → 23.3 of 55). Both improvers wrote answer keys without seeing the rubric. Spend since approval about $126.

harness2: It helps where there is headroom and does nothing where there is none, and it knows the difference: it kept the base harness on all 9 Claude Code tasks.
Its edits are process: a domain skill with a tested script, a trigger line, and rules like 'write the deliverable early'. On a weak model that is the whole gap.
Gains are per task family. A harness tuned on an easy task did not transfer to medium or hard ones; plan one adaptation per workflow.
It memorises when it can. Verifier-free does not mean leak-free: audit every adopted harness for answers and instance ids.
Some failures need enforcement, not instructions: a model that computes the answer but forgets to write it needs a hook.
On rubric-graded professional work the gain is small and partly format: held-out LAB gains came mostly from teaching the deliverable shape the judge reads.
A small model improving its own harness can make it worse: Haiku as its own improver lost 10 of 55 checks on the demo legal task.
benchmarking: Calibrate first. Two pilots at ceiling saved hours of meaningless runs.
Run an A/A check. It is the only reason we caught a fake +0.11 gain.
Classify infrastructure failures by content, not status codes. 'Not logged in' arrived as success.
Review before running. Three adversarial reviewers caught a silent blocker and seven grader bugs before any treatment result existed.
Pre-register and amend in public. Four amendments, each written before the affected results.
Sandbox model-driven processes: they will look around (190 blocked 'ls ..'), and the environment held real tokens.
Verifier-free improvement needs a train/test split by instance: score a harness on data its improver never saw, and treat in-task gains as test-time adaptation.
Diagnostic commands have side effects: `docker ps` started a VM that took two cores on a saturated host.
Every new artifact is a new leak path: version control put the graders into .git, readable from agent workspaces. Re-check the sandbox after any change to the project layout.
Verify credentials from the exact environment the runs use: a login that worked in one terminal still read 'not logged in' from the app's processes.
claude_code: Haiku 5.5 inside Claude Code already solved every tier here; measure before optimising a harness.
Harness² components map onto CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills, scripts, .claude/agents and hooks.
Nested claude -p needs isolation flags, an env allow-list and staggered starts to stay reproducible.
